claims.text: Equiatomic W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 can be fabricated by LPBF from mixed elemental powders through in-situ alloy formation.
LPBF provides rapid solidification during fabrication of the proposed W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 alloy.
A linear energy density of approximately 2.83 J/mm can produce complete fusion and greater than 99.8% relative density in W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20.
Mixed elemental or gas-atomized refractory-metal powders typically contain high concentrations of C, N, and O interstitial impurities.
High interstitial impurity content creates a propensity for brittle intermetallic phases or continuous ordered B2 networks during solidification.
As-built LPBF W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 can exhibit a single BCC phase.
Stepwise aging below the matrix solvus will induce coherent nanoprecipitations in LPBF W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20.
The induced coherent nanoprecipitations will specifically be discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure prevents formation of a continuous ordered B2 matrix associated with poor room-temperature ductility.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that cause premature crack initiation.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed coherent B2 precipitates will mitigate brittleness caused specifically by C, N, and O interstitial impurities.
The processed alloy will have tensile strength greater than 2.15 GPa and ambient-temperature tensile ductility in excess of 10-15%.
The alloy will retain significant tensile ductility and ultrahigh strength at temperatures up to 800 °C.
Refractory HEAs with a continuous ordered B2 matrix typically have high yield strength but poor room-temperature ductility.
Conventional arc-melted or gas-atomized refractory HEAs typically possess a two-phase B2+BCC structure with a continuous B2 matrix.
Interstitial concentrations exceeding their solubility limit would prevent the proposed strategy from mitigating brittleness.
An aging temperature that causes incoherent precipitate growth would invalidate the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes the desired state to stepwise aging, but the falsification rule declares the hypothesis false if the standard-aging control also fails. Failure of the control is expected under the proposed causal comparison and does not logically falsify the benefit of stepwise aging.
